newsitem.title: USA: Kellogg Q1 sales, margins below target - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Kellogg Q1 sales, margins below target - analysts.

text.p: Kellogg Co's first quarter sales and margins were weaker than projected, although its earnings were in line with expectations, analysts said.
"Sales are weaker than I expected," Goldman Sachs analyst Nomi Ghez said. "I thought that with the Lenders' aquisition, it would be a smaller decline."

Kellogg reported a 5.4 percent drop in net sales to $1.69 billion from $1.79 billion. Kellogg said its global sales volume rose 10 percent in the quarter, including Lender's bagels, which was acquired in December 1996.
Kellogg reported first quarter earnings of $0.77 a share that, as the company had projected, were below year-ago results of $0.99 a share before a $0.03 charge.

BT Securities analyst John O'Neil said Kellogg's margins were weaker than he anticipated. "Margins were a little lower than expected. Part of that is probably attributable to the integration of Lender's," he added.

Kellogg's first quarter faced a tough comparison with a year ago, when sales volumes were helped by promotions, O'Neil said. In addition, the 1996 first quarter was the last period before Kellogg cut its ready-to-eat cereal prices.
Kellogg said today it expects sales and earnings growth to return in the second quarter.
"It has to be, given the fact that the second quarter last year was so horrendous with sales down seven percent," Ghez said.

Kellogg's 1996 second quarter sales dropped to $1.65 billion from $1.78 billion. Second quarter 1996 earnings before charges fell to $0.45 a share from $0.77 a year before. The 1996 second quarter was the first period to reflect the reduction in cereal prices.
